column2: The Gayatri-singers sing to you, the hymn-makers hymn the hymn; the Brahmins, O hundred-powered, have raised you up like a bamboo pole.
The songs have strengthened Indra, who is wide as the ocean, the best of charioteers, lord of strengths, lord of the good.
Drink this pressed soma, Indra, this eldest immortal exhilaration; the streams of the bright one have flowed to you in the seat of truth.
Whatever wondrous wealth, Indra, is not here with me, which is given by you, O stone-bearer — bring that wealth, Vasu, with both hands.
Hear the call of him, Indra, who worships you with crooked ways; fill us with heroic wealth and cattle; you are great.
The soma has been pressed for you, Indra; come, O strongest, bold one; may the vital power fill you, as the sun fills the space with rays.
Come, Indra, with your bay horses to the fair praise of Kanva; go to heaven, to that heaven that rules, O Vasu of the day.
The songs have mounted you at the pressings like charioteers, O lover of songs; they have praised you together, as cows their calf.
Come, let us praise Indra, the pure, with a pure song; with pure hymns he grows; may he rejoice with pure blessings.
Whatever soma is most rich in wealth, whatever is most splendid in splendor — that soma, pressed for you, Indra, is an exhilaration, O lord of the offering.
Bring everything in turn to him, the knower, who wishes to drink; to the ready, the active, the one who goes forward and not back, O men.
You have driven away the fierce word that lies in the hollows, the great, in the early abodes, the great one that lies in life.
We turn you toward help and favor like a chariot — the strong-acting, helper, bountiful, mightiest Indra, lord of the good.
He, the ancient, great, loving, has been glorified by rites; at whose door Manu, the father, among the gods has glorified his prayers.
When the swift ones carry him shining in the chariots, drinking the joyful honey, there they make fame.
I praise him of yours, the unyielding lord of strength, Indra, the all-conquering man, the most able, the all-knowing.
I have sung of Dadhikravan, the victorious, swift horse; may he make our faces fragrant and prolong our lives.
The breaker of forts, young, wise, of measureless strength was born — Indra, the upholder of all work, wielder of the thunderbolt, much praised.
Offer to the delightful hero, to the soma, the food and the Trishtubh song; he honors it with devout thought, with abundance, for the gaining of wisdom.
Of Kashyapa, finder of heaven, they say the two are well yoked, whose every rite and sacrifice the wise have observed.
Sing, sing forth, men; the Priyamedhas sing; let the little sons sing; sing to the bold fort.
A hymn, worthy of praise, strengthening, for Indra of many wins; so that the mighty one may delight in our pressings and friendships.
I call for help the lord of wealth of Vishvanara, of unbending strength, and the chariots of the peoples.
He indeed, O heavenly one, the mortal who by devout thought and effort pleases you — by your help he crosses over hatred and sin from great heaven.
Pervading is your bounty, Indra, pervading your gift, O hundred-powered; so, all-seeing one, O good giver, exalt our splendor.
Even the birds, the two-footed, four-footed, flew up, O bright Dawn, following the seasons, from the ends of heaven.
You gods who are there in the middle of heaven's light — what is your truth, what your immortality, what is your ancient offering?
We worship the Rik and the Saman, by which they perform rites; in your assembly they shine and carry the sacrifice among the gods.
The men together fashioned Indra, overcomer of all armies, and begot him to reign; for the best deed, in a firm position — wide, fierce, mightiest, swift, speedy.
I place trust in you, in your first wrath, when you slew the Dasyu and uncovered the manly waters; when both worlds ran after you, even the earth, O stone-bearer, from fear of your might.
All assemble by strength around the lord of heaven who alone is guest of the peoples; the ancient, the new victor — to him alone the paths have turned.
We, Indra, are yours, O much-praised, we who move having begun with you, O lord of wealth; for no other than you, O lover of songs, sustains songs as the lands do; welcome our word.
The songs, great and worthy of hymn, have praised Indra, upholder of peoples, the bounteous; the one growing, invoked by many, with good praises, immortal, praised day by day.
The prayers desirous of heaven, together, all longing, have sung to Indra; they embrace him as wives their husband, the bounteous one, for help, as a bridegroom the pure.
Honor with songs that ram, much invoked, worthy of the Rik, Indra, the ocean of wealth, whose mighty ones do not move apart from men; praise the greatest sage for food.
Honor well that ram, finder of heaven, whose hundred good beings stir together; I turn Indra for help with fair praises, like a racing horse, a chariot flowing to the call.
Rich in ghee, adorning the worlds, wide, broad, milking honey, fair-formed — heaven and earth, held apart by the law of Varuna, unaging, of abundant seed.
When, Indra, you filled both worlds like the dawn — great, sovereign of the great ones, of the peoples; the divine mother bore you; the auspicious mother bore you.
Offer a food-laden word to the delighted one, who with Rijishvan slew the black-wombed; we, desiring help, call the bull, thunderbolt in his right hand, with the Maruts, for friendship.
Indra, among the pressed somas you purify the wisdom worthy of praise; he is great, for he knows the strengthening skill.
Sing to him, the much-invoked, the much-praised; honor Indra with songs, mighty one.
We praise that exhilaration of yours, the bull, victorious in battle, O stone-bearer, the world-maker, the beauty of the bay horses.
When, Indra, you rejoice in the soma in Vishnu, or in Trita Aptya, or among the Maruts, together with the drops.
Pour out, O Adhvaryu, the most exhilarating of the honeyed drink; so is the hero praised, ever growing.
Pour the drop for Indra; he drinks the soma honey; by his greatness he urges on gifts.
Come, friends, let us praise Indra, the praiseworthy man, who alone overcomes all peoples.
Sing the great Saman to Indra, the wise, the great, the prayer-maker, the sage, the wonder-worker.
He who alone distributes wealth to the giving mortal, the ruler, not to be gainsaid — indeed Indra.
Friends, we bring prayer to Indra, the thunderbolt-bearer; I praise him well, your best of men, the bold.
I praise that strength of yours, Indra, the highest, for the worship of the gods, by which you slay Vritra with might, O lord of power.
Who in joy cooked Shambara for Divodasa — this soma, Indra, is pressed for you; drink.
Come to us, dear Indra, the ever-victorious, unhidden, broad like a mountain on all sides, lord of heaven.
The most soma-drinking exhilaration, strongest Indra, which is perceived, by which you slay the devourer — we seek that.
For our children and grandchildren, and for living, grant us a long life, O Adityas, equal in splendor.
You know, thunderbolt-handed, the encircling of the Nirritis; day by day pure as a cleansing of the paths.
Drive away disease, drive away the oppressor, drive away evil thought; O Adityas, free us from distress.
Drink the soma, Indra; may it delight you, which the stone pressed for you, O bay-horsed one, held by the arms of the presser like a horse.
Without a rival, without kin, you, Indra, have been forever by nature; for battle you wish for kinship.
Of him who in the past brought us this and that gift, I praise him; friends, for help, Indra.
Come, do not do harm; do not stand aloof, you who share one spirit, firm, restraining.
Come, for the drop, O lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fields; drink the soma, lord of soma.
With you as our ally, O bull, we would speak to the snorting foe in the assembly of the people with cattle.
Even the cows with one mind, the Maruts with kinsmen, lick the peaks one another.
Bring us, Indra, strength and manly power, O hundred-powered, all-seeing, a hero who overcomes armies.
So now, O lover of songs, Indra, we approach you with desire; we come together like waters flowing to waters.
We sit like birds around you in the cow-sweetened, intoxicating honey, to carry you; to you, Indra, we cry aloud.
We, O unprecedented, bring to you like a pillar nothing, longing for help; O thunderbolt-bearer, we call on the wonderful.
The fair-skinned ones drink of the sweet, all-spread honey, who with Indra, the bull, are joyful, beautiful, wealthy, according to self-rule.
So indeed soma is the exhilaration; it made prayer the increase; O strongest thunderbolt-bearer, with might you slew the serpent from the earth, praising according to self-rule.
Indra grew for exhilaration and strength, the Vritra-slayer with men; him, great in battles, we call in the small as well; may he protect us in the contests.
To you, Indra, O stone-bearer, thunderbolt-wielder, belongs the unrestrained heroism; when you slew that deceitful beast by your magic, praising according to self-rule.
Go forth, attack, be bold; your thunderbolt does not fail; your strength, Indra, is manliness; you slew Vritra and won the waters, praising according to self-rule.
When contests arise, wealth is set for the bold; yoke your two bay horses that drop exhilaration; whom do you slay, in whose wealth do you place us, Indra?
They have eaten and rejoiced, and shaken off their dear ones; the sages of self-radiance have praised with new thought; Indra, your bay horses are yoked.
Listen well to our songs, bounteous one, like a mother; when will you make us rich in truth and kindness? Your bay horses are yoked, Indra.
The moon flies among the waters, the fair-winged bird in the sky; the golden-rimmed lightnings do not find your resting-place; know this, O heaven and earth.
Your best-loved chariot, the bull, carrier of wealth, O Ashvins — the singer adorns it with hymns; O honeyed ones, hear my call.
O Agni, we kindle your shining, ageless splendor, O god; may your most worthy kindling blaze; bring to the singers the heavenly gift.
We choose you, the priest, like Agni, with good praises — the hero of pure flame, in your joy at the sacrifices, who spread the grass, you carry.
Awaken us today to great wealth, O Dawn of heaven, as you have awakened us, true-famed, O Vayya, well-born, bringer of horses and good speech.
Bring auspicious things to us; stir our mind, skill and wisdom; then in your friendship, in the joy of the drink, we shall delight, like cows in pasture, you carry.
By skill the great one, in accordance with his own power, the terrible strength has returned; the splendid, fair-lipped, bay-horsed one holds in his hands the iron thunderbolt for glory.
He indeed mounts that bull-chariot which finds cattle, who, O Indra, is aware of the bay-yoked vessel full; your two bay horses are yoked.
I consider Agni the one who is wealth, to whom the cows come home; home the swift horses, home the steadfast strong ones; bring food to the singers.
Neither sin nor evil, O gods, reaches the mortal whom Aryaman, Mitra and Varuna, in agreement, lead past hatred.
Flow around, O Soma, for Indra, sweet, for Mitra, Pushan and Bhaga.
Flow well around for the winning of strength; overcoming Vritras all around; you pass over the enemies, you drive us to pay debts.
Flow, Soma, great ocean, father of the gods, to all realms.
Flow, Soma, for great skill, like a decked horse, strong, for wealth.
The drop has been purified, fair, for delight, the seer in the lap of the waters, for good fortune.
We have rejoiced in you, pressed Soma, for great sovereignty in the battle; as you flow, you plunge into strengths.
Who are these manifest men of one nest, the heroes of Rudra, the well-horsed?
O Agni, today we make you succeed with praises as a horse, like auspicious wisdom touching the heart, with our offerings.
The mortal-heroes, the strong, have come to the strength, to the impulse of the god Savitar; win heavens, O horses.
Flow, Soma, splendid, with fair streams, great, first among the sheep.
O giver on all sides, bring to us on all sides what we ask of you, the strongest.
This is the prayer, the seasonal; I praise Indra, the famed by name.
The Brahmins, exalting Indra with hymns, strengthened him to slay the serpent.
They fashioned a chariot for your horse, and Tvashtar the shining thunderbolt, O much-invoked.
The one who desires wealth sends forth his wish for the auspicious place and bounty; the lawless one does not approach wealth.
